clue.text: Carriage replacing phaetons

indicators.note: replacing suggests the letters of the following word are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A new carriage is brought in to take the place of old phaetons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' looks like plain surface sense, but it is the anagram signal working on PHAETONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn vehicle with one seat, named after the clergyman who first had one built.

clue.text: Portion of Christmas pudding for King Edward, say

indicators.note: a portion of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A slice of Christmas pudding is set aside for a king called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is not a monarch here but a popular British variety of potato; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is informal for potato, and King Edward is a well-known potato variety.

clue.text: Just open a glass of beer

parts.note: in British slang a jar is a glass of beer, as in 'going for a jar'

explanation.surface: Someone has only just cracked open a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open, not shut and not wide, is described this way.

clue.text: Case he had mishandled, leading to complaints at the top

indicators.note: something mishandled is botched, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A badly handled case leads to grievances being raised with senior management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints at the top' reads as grumbles to the bosses, but means ailments of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Pains in the head are ailments, or complaints, located at the top of the body.

clue.text: A student of swinging Britain, for example

definitions.text: A student of swinging Britain, for example

parts.words: A student of swinging Britain, for example
parts.note: sounds like a historian of the swinging sixties, but means someone who analyses electoral swings, such as those in British general elections

explanation.surface: An academic researching the swinging London scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging Britain' evokes the 1960s; it actually means Britain's swings in voting from party to party.
explanation.definitionFit: Psephology is the scientific study of elections and voting trends, including swings between parties.

clue.text: Follow member to this hole

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A golfer is told to keep going and walk on to this particular hole.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, a hole whose fairway bends sharply is named after the angle of a dog's hind limb.

clue.text: Duck with sour smell

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, which looks like the letter O
sour, meaning grim and unsmiling, gives dour

explanation.surface: A duck has a sour, unpleasant smell about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter out without scoring has made a 'duck', i.e. zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour is a synonym for smell or scent.

clue.text: Learner joining a new college with grounds

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
Downing is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A trainee joins a newly founded college that has extensive grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' is just a link; DOWNING is a Cambridge college, which suits the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning land is having property or estates, that is, being possessed of grounds.

clue.text: One of younger generation rebuked about loss initially under 1000

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

indicators.note: initially means take just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A youngster is scolded for losing money, with the loss under a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' is a positional indicator in a down clue: the thousand sits above the rest. 'about' and 'initially' are container and first-letter signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandchild belongs to the generation two below oneself, so is one of the younger generation.

clue.text: Inadvertently, university was near disaster

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so these letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A university came close to calamity without realising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' reads as a noun in the surface, but it is the anagram signal for WASNEAR, giving NAWARES.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught unawares is to be taken by surprise, without knowing or intending.

clue.text: Feebly humorous material each viewer sees through

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental or feeble humour

explanation.surface: Every audience member can see past the weak jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewer' is the eye, not a TV audience; the definition is the part of the eye that light passes through.
explanation.definitionFit: The transparent front layer of the eye is what the eye, as a viewer, looks through.

clue.text: Traveller comes to regret getting blotto at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A traveller regrets getting thoroughly drunk on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits a sailor's binge but signals an anagram of REGRET and BLOTTO; 'blotto' is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who travels the world widely is known as a globe-trotter.

clue.text: Position of men not yet in recognised union

definitions.text: Position of men not yet in recognised union

parts.words: Position of men not yet in recognised union
parts.note: reads like a remark about unofficial trade unions, but describes the state of men who have not yet married

explanation.surface: A complaint about workers not yet in an officially recognised trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'recognised union' sounds industrial; it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being an unmarried man is the condition of a man not yet wed.

clue.text: Collaring business initially without loud talking

indicators.note: initially means this piece goes at the front of the rest

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to nab them
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A business arrests someone at first without making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'initially' says which piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To confab is to chat informally, so this means chatting or talking.

clue.text: Home, nursing ' temperature? Take pulse!

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: the hearth is the fireside, standing for the home
to rob is to take unlawfully

explanation.surface: A nurse at home checks the patient's temperature and pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take pulse' looks like a medical order, but 'Take' gives ROB and 'pulse' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb of the heart is a single beat, the old literal sense of the word, matching a pulse.

clue.text: Honour a husband - .that's a charming practice

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: Giving a husband an award is described as a delightful custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charming' sounds like 'delightful' but means casting charms, i.e. magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of sorcery or folk magic practised in the Caribbean, a practice of casting spells.

clue.text: Intricate arrangement that's needed to maintain one's balance

definitions.meaning: a maze, a complicated network of paths

definitions.text: that's needed to maintain one's balance
definitions.meaning: the inner ear, whose canals govern the sense of balance

explanation.surface: Something complicated is required just to keep steady.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a maze and the bony cavity of the inner ear that controls equilibrium.

clue.text: Sort of heat people having rows may generate

definitions.text: Sort of heat people having rows may generate

parts.words: Sort of heat people having rows may generate
parts.note: suggests heated quarrels, but means a race heat for oarsmen, those who row boats

explanation.surface: People who argue a lot tend to generate a lot of heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' rhymes with 'cows' in the surface but rhymes with 'goes' in the solution: rowers' heats.
explanation.definitionFit: A repechage is an extra qualifying heat in rowing and other sports that gives losers a second chance.

clue.text: Looking ahead because seamen's leader is cutting the crew

parts.note: for can mean because, as in 'for he was tired'

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside the other piece

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: Being far-sighted, the senior sailor reduces the size of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests cutbacks but means inserting; 'leader' takes only the first letter of seamen's.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the ability to anticipate and plan for what lies ahead.

clue.text: Place for instruments, a dozen in a box

definitions.meaning: the instrument board or control fascia of a car or aircraft
a jury, twelve people seated in the jury box

explanation.surface: A box holds twelve musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a board of dials and gauges and the list of people serving on a jury.

clue.text: Fat wedge of brittle sweet

parts.note: butter is a fat
a scotch is a wedge or block put under a wheel to stop it rolling

explanation.surface: A thick slice of crunchy confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard, brittle toffee made from butter and brown sugar.

clue.text: Cancel article in old-fashioned language

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic languages of Scotland and Ireland
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written in archaic language is withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to delete or wipe out, so to cancel.

clue.text: Write up a useful hint for making bread

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing words upwards means they read backwards from bottom to top

parts.note: a tip is a useful hint or piece of advice

explanation.surface: Someone writes up a handy tip for baking bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write up' reverses A TIP as a whole, giving PIT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta, or pita, is a flat bread originating in the Middle East.

clue.text: I had heard and watched

indicators.note: heard means the words are said out loud and spelt as a word that sounds the same

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having listened and looked on.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it, so this past form means looked at or watched.

clue.text: Attack as unsafe place for children to play

definitions.meaning: an incursion or raid into enemy territory

definitions.text: as unsafe place for children to play
definitions.meaning: read as two words, out on the street, where traffic makes play dangerous

explanation.surface: A warning that playing on the street is dangerous for children.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is a hostile incursion, and split in two it says children are out on the highway.

clue.text: Way to endorse structure in hierarchy

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ratify is to approve formally or endorse

explanation.surface: A method of approving the structure of an organisation's ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To stratify is to arrange in layers or social ranks, ordering into a hierarchy.

clue.text: Mouth with impediment needed special drinking vessel

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A person with a speech impediment needs a special cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a bowl-shaped glass with a stem, often used for wine or ceremonial drinking.

clue.text: On the house, worker has carte blanche

parts.note: on the house means given without charge, so free
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer is given free rein, all paid for by the employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a free hand means unrestricted authority to act, the same as carte blanche.
